A day of 100% focus at the White House.

Bessent was laser focused on using economic power against Iran.

Trump was no less focused, but his target was Canada.

Americans hear "51st state" as Trump trolling. Canadians hear it as an existential threat to their sovereignty. That gap in perception is why Carney can't afford to look conciliatory, even if the economics of retaliation don't add up. This isn't just a trade war anymore.

My insta-analysis of Operation Economic Outcast -- economic D-Day -- asks what the U.S. can learn from its past adventures with sanctions (ahem, Cuba), and what careful studies say about the likelihood that the Administration will achieve its goals.
www.youtube.com/watch?v=tOu7...

The market's verdict on the announcement of Operation Economic Outcast was to shrug its shoulders and act as if no-one said anything of any relevance to anything.

Makes you think.
